findings.claim: g5 root cause: chat history is self._messages on the SynapsePanel QWidget (dies on close), runtime is a per-send ClaudeWorker QThread parent=self (not rebound on reopen), no save/restore; COMPOUNDED by the pypanel loader flushing sys.modules[synapse.*] on every reopen (resets any module singleton). Fix: disk-backed store outside the synapse.* namespace.

R.3 dependency (out of scope): the pypanel sys.modules[synapse.*] flush also resets runtime_beat._timer on reopen, so a post-flush ensure_beat_started() arms a SECOND parentless QTimer while the old one keeps beating — harmless for freeze detection (more liveness, never fewer) but leaks one timer per reopen. runtime_beat stays hou-free + idempotent within a module lifetime; the disk store is flush-proof by construction. Perfect reopen idempotency of the beat needs R.3 (gate the purge).

Restoring self._messages at __init__ restores the MODEL's conversation (the next turn continues the same session), but does NOT repaint the visible chat bubbles on reopen — that is deeper GUI wiring (rebuild the transcript view from restored messages), hard to verify headless. Session STATE survives; the visible restore is a follow-up (spawn).

Test contracts SUPERSEDED (not weakened) by R.2's validated design: test_freeze_chain.py closeEvent source-pin now asserts detach_panel present + shutdown_freeze_chain absent; test_r_track.py moves runtime_owns_heartbeat from the RED-on-live tuple to the GREEN-exceptions list (deps_isolated precedent); test_panel_freeze_beat.py repointed from panel-owns-_freeze_timer to the owner contract. The old 'closeEvent must shut the chain down' invariant is exactly what R.2 replaces with a live process-lifetime beat.

SHARED reconciliation point flagged for peers: tests/test_r_track.py::test_live_tree_gates_read_red_now lists every unresolved P0 gate as RED-on-live. Any leg that RESOLVES a gate (e.g. W5-SHELF resolving shelf_current) must move it out of the SAME tuple hunk -> serialize on this file via the bus or merge-conflict on that hunk.

Test isolation: runtime_beat._QT_AVAILABLE is set at import; under the full suite a sibling test's Qt stub is in sys.modules when runtime_beat first imports, flipping it True. The headless heartbeat test now pins _qapp_instance -> None in an autouse fixture and no longer asserts the ambient _QT_AVAILABLE flag, so it is order-independent.
